label: Indian qualifications accepted for undergraduate entry
value: CBSE (AISSC) or CISCE (ISC) Class XII; state board results considered individually. No minimum percentage is published on this page.
passage: All India Senior School Certificate (awarded by CBSE) or Indian School Certificate (awarded by CISCE). Year 12 State Board Exams with excellent results will also be considered on an individual basis.
notes: Country page lists qualifications only, no percentage. Separate note: CBSE applicants to calculus-requiring programmes need Class XII Standard Mathematics (Applied Mathematics not accepted).

label: CBSE maths for calculus-based programmes
value: Class XII Standard Mathematics required; Applied Mathematics does not meet the calculus requirement
passage: CBSE students interested in programs that require Calculus for admission, such as business, engineering, and science programs, must present Class XII Standard Mathematics for admission consideration. Class XII Applied Mathematics (new and old syllabus) will not meet the Calculus requirement.

label: IELTS Academic for undergraduate entry
value: Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0
passage: The minimum requirement is an overall band of 6.5, with no band below 6.0.
notes: India is not on the page's list of countries that may qualify for exemption; exemptions are decided after applying.

label: Can Class XII English replace a test?

passage: No. A senior-level English course is required for admission, but it does not meet the English language proficiency requirement.
notes: Answer to the FAQ "Can I submit my Grade 12 English course instead of a language test?"

label: Class XII (CBSE/ISC) for undergraduate entry
value: Normally 75%–87% on in-progress grades, 80%–91% on final Class XII results, depending on programme
passage: The minimum requirements are overall averages and prerequisite subject requirements normally between 75% to the 87% on in-progress grades and depending on the program applied to. notes: Minimums do not guarantee admission. Reviewed on a minimum of four academic courses.
